Question
========
You have a data frame `d` with 10 rows. You run `d[1:2] <- 1:3` (attempting to replace the first two columns using a
length-3 replacement vector), and R raises an error. Why?

Answerlist
----------
* Because replacing 2 columns of 10 rows needs 20 values total, and 3 does not evenly divide 20, so R can't recycle
  the replacement vector without leaving a "leftover," ambiguous partial fill.
* Because you can never use a numeric vector to replace data frame columns.
* Because `d[1:2] <-` can only ever replace exactly one column at a time.
* Because 3 is larger than 2 (the number of columns being replaced).
* Because the replacement vector must always be named.

Solution
========
Just like with vectors and matrices, R recycles a shorter replacement vector to fill a longer selection, but only
when the replacement length evenly divides the total number of values needed. Replacing 2 columns across 10 rows
requires 20 values, and a length-3 vector doesn't divide 20 evenly (20 / 3 isn't a whole number), so R refuses rather
than guessing at an ambiguous fill pattern.
